title: How to Make Money From Instagram Reels in 2026 (Does Instagram Pay for Reels?)
excerpt: Does Instagram pay for Reels, and how do small creators actually earn from them? The 6 ways to make money from Instagram Reels in 2026, and which ones work first.
content:
Does Instagram pay you for Reels?

Quick answer: in most countries Instagram does not pay a standard rate per view for Reels. Instagram has run invite-only Reels bonus programs at times and offers features like Gifts and subscriptions where available, but most creators who earn from Reels do it through brand deals, UGC, and affiliate links. For small creators, brand deals and UGC are usually the first real income.

How do you make money from Instagram Reels?

MethodWho it suitsNeeds a big audience?
Brand deals (sponsored Reels)Creators with a clear nicheNo, micro-creators get them
UGC (videos brands post or run as ads)Anyone who films products wellNo
Affiliate links and codesProduct and recommendation contentHelps, but not required
Gifts from viewersCreators whose Reels get regular viewsWhere the feature is available
SubscriptionsCreators with a loyal communityUsually yes
Bonuses from InstagramInvited creators onlyDepends on the program

1. Brand deals: the main way Reels pay

A brand pays you (or sends free product) to make a Reel about their product and post it on your account with the Paid partnership label. Brands care about niche fit and whether your Reels show a product well more than follower count. Most small creators get their first deals by pitching brands directly by email with one specific video idea. See our guide on how to get sponsorship deals on Instagram.

2. UGC: get paid for the video, not your followers

With UGC, the brand pays you to create the Reel and then posts it on its own account or runs it as an ad. Your audience size barely matters, which makes it the fastest route for small creators. Charge per video and add a fee for ad usage rights.

3. Affiliate links and discount codes

You earn a commission when viewers buy through your link or code. It works best for honest product recommendations and roundups ("3 things I actually reuse"). Expect small amounts at first; it grows with consistent posting in one niche.

4. Gifts and subscriptions

Where available, viewers can send you Gifts on Reels, and followers can pay a monthly subscription for exclusive content. These usually need an engaged audience before they add up, so treat them as extras, not your first income.

5. Bonuses from Instagram

Instagram has offered invite-only bonus programs for Reels in some countries. You can't apply for most of them; if you're invited, you'll see it in your professional dashboard. Don't plan your income around them.

6. Turn Reels into a portfolio

Every good Reel is also proof for your next pitch. Keep your three best product Reels pinned and link them in a simple portfolio or media kit so brands can judge your work in seconds.

What should a small creator do first?

  1. Pick one niche and post Reels consistently.
  2. Make three Reels that show products you own the way an ad would.
  3. Pitch five to ten growing brands a week by email with one idea each, and follow up.
  4. Add affiliate links to products you genuinely recommend.

faq.question: Does Instagram pay for Reels views?
faq.answer: Not as a standard per-view rate in most countries. Instagram has offered invite-only Reels bonuses at times and supports Gifts and subscriptions where available, but most creators earn from Reels through brand deals, UGC and affiliate links.

faq.question: How many followers do you need to make money on Instagram Reels?
faq.answer: None for brand deals you pitch or for UGC, where brands pay for the video itself. Features like subscriptions and some bonus programs have their own eligibility rules and usually need a larger, engaged audience.

faq.question: What is the fastest way for a small creator to earn from Reels?
faq.answer: UGC and gifted or paid brand collaborations. Make a few Reels that show products well, then pitch growing brands in your niche by email with one specific idea and links to your best Reels.

faq.question: Can you earn money from Reels with affiliate links?
faq.answer: Yes. You earn a commission when viewers buy through your link or code. It works best for honest recommendations in a clear niche and grows with consistent posting.

faq.question: Do I need to label paid Reels?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Instagram's Paid partnership label for sponsored or gifted Reels. In the US the FTC expects clear disclosure of any material connection with a brand.
